headline: Custer Gallatin National Forest and Museum Entry Checks
reservation: While Bozeman itself is an open city, specialized guided rafting on the Gallatin or Madison rivers requires advance booking with private outfitters. Visitors planning to enter nearby Yellowstone National Park must check the official NPS site for current entry reservation systems and road closures. Museum of the Rockies recommends purchasing timed tickets online during peak summer months to ensure entry; always verify current policies at official sources.

days.title: Foothills and University Culture

stops.name: Peets Hill at Burke Park
stops.detail: Walk the gentle bluff trails for panoramic views of the Gallatin Valley and surrounding mountain ranges.

stops.name: Museum of the Rockies
stops.detail: Explore extensive paleontological exhibits including one of the world's largest collections of Tyrannosaurus rex fossils.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for local transfers; conditions vary by season
days.note: Peets Hill trails can be icy or muddy in spring; stick to established paths.

days.title: Canyon Vistas and Higher Elevations

stops.name: The College M Trail
stops.detail: Choose between the steep or winding path to the iconic letter for views of the Bridger Range.

stops.name: Gallatin Canyon Pullouts
stops.detail: Drive south toward Big Sky, stopping only at designated turnouts to view the Gallatin River safely.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours round trip; mountain roads may have lingering snow
days.note: Start early to secure limited trailhead parking at the M trail.

days.title: River Valleys and Historic Main Street

stops.name: Main Street to the Mountains
stops.detail: Utilize the town's connected trail system for a low-impact walk through leafy neighborhoods.

stops.name: Gallatin History Museum
stops.detail: Visit the former county jail to learn about the regional pioneer and agricultural history.

days.driving: Walking and local transfers suggested; traffic varies
days.note: Downtown parking is metered; check local signage for time limits.

intel.title: Downtown and Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Parking in central Bozeman is managed by timed kiosks; trailheads like the M fill rapidly on summer mornings. Have a backup trailhead in mind as narrow shoulders are often tow-away zones.

intel.title: Canyon Communication Gaps
intel.text: Cellular reception is reliable in Bozeman and Belgrade but often drops entirely within Gallatin Canyon. Download offline maps before heading south toward Big Sky or West Yellowstone.

intel.title: Valley Supply Points
intel.text: Major fueling stations are concentrated in Bozeman, Belgrade, and Four Corners. Supply options decrease significantly once you enter the Custer Gallatin National Forest corridors.

intel.title: Seasonal Trail Access
intel.text: Higher elevation routes like those in the Bridgers may hold snow until July. Check the Custer Gallatin National Forest site for mud season closures to avoid damaging trails.

intel.title: River Public Access
intel.text: Rivers are bordered by private land; only use official fishing access sites (FAS) managed by the state. Respect all posted signage regarding boat launches and private property boundaries.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at BZN, stock up on supplies in Belgrade or Four Corners, and check into valley lodgings before exploring Main Street.
plan.vehicle: A standard car suits town, but a high-clearance vehicle is recommended for forest service roads; check rental restrictions for unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Peets Hill offers expansive sunset views over the valley, though cloud cover in the Tobacco Root Mountains varies seasonally.
